step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows a multi-account centralized logging solution across an 'Individual Acct' and a 'Centralized Acct'. In the Individual Account, logs are generated from EC2 (sending logs to CloudWatch), CloudTrail, and VPC Flow Logs. These three sources feed into Kinesis Firehose, which forwards data to a Lambda function for log transformation and filtering. This Lambda writes the processed logs to a centralized S3 bucket in the Centralized Account. When new log objects land in S3, they trigger a second Lambda function in the Centralized Account, which ingests and indexes the data into Elasticsearch (mapped to OpenSearch). Kibana (mapped to ThirdParty) is positioned alongside Elasticsearch for visualization and log analysis.

edges.notes: EC2 application sends logs to CloudWatch agent
CloudWatch streams logs to Kinesis Firehose
CloudTrail pushes audit logs to Kinesis Firehose
Flow Logs pushes network logs to Kinesis Firehose
Kinesis Firehose sends stream data to Lambda
Lambda writes converted logs cross-account into S3
S3 object creation triggers centralized Lambda
Lambda pushes ingested logs to Elasticsearch
Elasticsearch provides backend search capabilities for Kibana visualization
